title: Integers, Fractions and Rational Numbers
summary: From temperatures below zero to sharing a pizza: integers, fractions and decimals, why negative × negative is positive, and the rational numbers that fill the number line.

ib.statementOfInquiry: The same quantity can be represented in many equivalent forms, and choosing the right form helps us compare, calculate and describe the world.

factual: How do we add, subtract, multiply and divide integers?
How do we compare and add fractions?
Which fractions have decimals that stop?
conceptual: Why does dividing by a fraction less than 1 give a bigger answer?
debatable: Was the invention of zero and negative numbers the most important idea in mathematics?
Are fractions or decimals more useful in everyday life?
